clue.text: Strong odour problem returns before week's end

indicators.note: before places the reversed problem ahead of the next piece
returns means the word for problem is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word week's

explanation.surface: A powerful smell problem keeps coming back as the week draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: The deer-gland perfume base is a classic example of a strong, heavy scent.

clue.text: Set up plan to guard pine arboretum's first tree

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the assembled letters are read upwards, backwards
to guard means the plan word surrounds the following letters

parts.note: an aim is a plan or intention
to pine is to long for something

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word arboretum's

explanation.surface: Planning to protect a pine as the arboretum's prime specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree but is the verb meaning to long; the tree is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering shrub or small tree is grown widely in gardens and arboreta.

clue.text: Nothing new in arch needing a brush-up?

indicators.note: in places nothing and new inside the arch word

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing
love means nothing or zero in tennis

explanation.surface: An architectural arch needing a fresh coat of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' looks structural but is the adjective meaning cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untidy and unkempt could do with a tidy-up or brush-up.

clue.text: Scottish island Eigg stripped after trouble with bones

indicators.note: after places the trimmed island last

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
sacra is the plural of sacrum, the bone at the base of the spine

indicators.note: stripped means the word Eigg loses its outer letters, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: An island off Scotland's west coast, stripped bare, follows some trouble with skeletal remains.
explanation.walkthrough: Eigg is itself a Scottish island, which makes it look like the definition; it is only fodder. AILSA CRAIG is a rocky islet in the Firth of Clyde, famous for curling stones.
explanation.definitionFit: This granite islet lies in the Firth of Clyde off the Ayrshire coast.

clue.text: First person caught leaving intimate, insincere statements

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs from the intimate word

parts.note: a crony is an intimate friend
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone close is caught out, leaving behind insincere words.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the opposite of what one means is a form of insincere or mocking expression.

clue.text: Bad options are hiding a vexing subject

indicators.note: bad means these letters are put in a poor, disordered state
hiding means the following a is kept out of sight, removed from the word are

explanation.surface: Poor choices conceal a touchy topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic that annoys or upsets someone whenever it is raised is a touchy, vexing subject.

clue.text: Banker entering African country: I'm doubtful he likes live music

indicators.note: entering means the banker goes inside the country

parts.note: the Congo is a country in Africa
a banker is a racing certainty, a cert
er is a hesitant noise expressing doubt

explanation.surface: A financier heading into Africa is unsure about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests money but means a sure bet, a CERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular at live performances of music is someone who attends concerts.

clue.text: I may obsess over stats and not area covered by Alaska

indicators.note: covered by means the Alaska letters go round the other pieces

parts.note: AK is the US postal code for Alaska
nor means and not

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on statistics, but not about the area Alaska covers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang an anorak is a nerdy obsessive, named after the waterproof jacket trainspotters wear.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nerdy obsessive, fixated on facts and figures, is this kind of person.

clue.text: Church music record involving extended play's sent heavenward

indicators.note: sent heavenward in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
involving means the record word contains the other

parts.note: a log is a written record
EPs are extended-play records, here with 's as is

explanation.surface: A recording of church music, extended play included, rises to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: This style of African-American Christian song is a form of church music.

clue.text: No such booze would repel a petrifying monster

definitions.text: No such booze would repel a petrifying monster

parts.words: No such booze would repel a petrifying monster
parts.note: write 'no' plus this drink, then turn the whole string round, and you get the snake-haired creature whose gaze turns people to stone

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek warning that this drink offers no protection against Medusa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repel' here means turn back: NO + the drink, reversed, spells GORGON, the petrifying monster. The drink is rum and water, a sailor's ration.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum diluted with water, the traditional naval ration, is a kind of booze.

clue.text: Dire note in brass instrument to meet our needs?

indicators.note: in places the note inside the instrument

parts.note: the horn is a brass instrument
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
something that will do us is enough to meet our needs

explanation.surface: A grim musical note sounds from a horn, though apparently it suits us.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dreadful or appalling.

clue.text: What's to follow, assuming sedentary period?

definitions.text: What's to follow, assuming sedentary period?

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the word for follow takes the sitting period inside it

parts.note: to obey is to follow orders
a sit is a period spent seated

explanation.surface: A question about what results from spending a long time sitting down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: weight gain is what follows a sedentary spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive body fat is the consequence the clue implies of too much sitting.

clue.text: Accepted by faction I have to embrace otherwise I might be a mole

parts.note: in means accepted, as in fashionable
a sect is a faction

indicators.note: to embrace means the contraction wraps round the next word

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have
or means otherwise

explanation.surface: An undercover agent accepted by a group, admitting he might be a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests espionage; here it is the burrowing animal that eats insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Moles feed on insects and worms, making them one example of a bug-eating mammal.

clue.text: Introduce rule enforcer, breaking step

indicators.note: breaking means the referee splits the step word open

parts.note: a pace is a single step
a ref (referee) enforces the rules of a game

explanation.surface: A referee interrupts a stride to bring something in.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a book or speech with remarks is to introduce it; the verb sense of a foreword.

clue.text: Badly tailored suits including one worn by tricky entertainer

parts.note: ill can mean badly, as in ill-judged

indicators.note: including means the reshaped suits wrap round the next pieces
tailored means the letters of suits are cut and reshaped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
clothes that are worn are on

explanation.surface: Poorly cut suits, one being worn by a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailored' looks like part of the clothing picture but is the anagram signal, and 'Badly' gives ILL rather than signalling an anagram itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjurer performs tricks of illusion, making them an entertainer who deceives the eye.

clue.text: Deepen nod, somehow inviting any response

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Nodding more deeply in some way to invite a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A question without fixed options invites any kind of answer.

clue.text: Get wine round to eat lentil dish, a spicy one

indicators.note: to eat means the wine and round letters take the lentil dish inside

parts.note: vino is informal for wine
dal is an Indian lentil dish
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Fetch a glass of wine to go with a lentil curry and a hot one.
explanation.definitionFit: This hot Indian curry is a notably spicy dish, one of several on the menu.

clue.text: Subject of medical research yet to have host almost replacing heart

indicators.note: replacing heart means the middle letter of the yet word is swapped out

parts.note: still means yet

indicators.note: almost means the host word loses its final letter

parts.note: an emcee is a host or master of ceremonies

explanation.surface: A medical topic awaiting a host after a heart transplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' sounds surgical but just means the middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Undifferentiated cells able to become other types are a major area of medical study.

clue.text: Adaptation of insect to air? I'll deny it

indicators.note: adaptation means changing form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insect evolving to fly prompts someone to deny that evolution happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adaptation' is an evolutionary word, and the 'it' denied is that very evolution, so the definition rides on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone believing in literal divine creation rejects evolutionary adaptation.

clue.text: Difficulty over Parisian water agency

indicators.note: over means the difficulty word is turned round

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A problem with water in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A government department or office such as the FBI is an agency.

clue.text: With you and me for the last couple, light on one's feet — or round one's head?

indicators.note: for the last couple means the final two letters are replaced

parts.note: nimble means light on one's feet
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A dancer, light on their feet, or perhaps a halo-wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on feet versus head: the saintly halo surrounds one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo depicted around a saint's head is this bright disc.

clue.text: Take advantage of some fires I lit up in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution means the selected letters are turned round
some means only part of the run of words fires I lit up is used

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a few blazes they set during an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To use or make use of something is to take advantage of it.

clue.text: Fashion to knock off reverses tedium

indicators.note: reverses means the combined words are read backwards

parts.note: a mode is a fashion
to knock off is slang for to steal or rob

explanation.surface: Stealing a fashion idea undoes the tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Weariness from lack of interest is a synonym for tedium.

clue.text: Pale green fruit with no core left

indicators.note: with no core means the middle letter of the fruit word is dropped

parts.note: a berry is a fruit

explanation.surface: A green fruit left with its core removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The aquamarine variety of this gemstone gives a name to a pale bluish-green colour.

clue.text: Couturier turns in glowing piece with variable decorative stitching

indicators.note: in places the reversed name inside the glowing piece

parts.note: an ember is a glowing piece of coal or wood

indicators.note: turns means the designer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A fashion designer twists something bright into fancy needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental needlework on fabric is exactly decorative stitching.

clue.text: Inclination to skip inauguration of President Bush

indicators.note: to skip means a letter is left out

parts.note: a slope is an incline

indicators.note: inauguration, the start of a term, picks the first letter of President

explanation.surface: A political leaning skipping the swearing-in of George Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Bush' reads as one name; Bush is in fact the definition, the blackthorn shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackthorn is a shrub that bears this sour fruit, so the plant itself is a bush.

clue.text: Dylan suite remixed without consistency?

indicators.note: remixed means the letters are mixed into a new order, as music is remixed

explanation.surface: A remix of a Bob Dylan suite turns out patchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a wobbly, irregular way means lacking consistency or steadiness.

clue.text: Fleshy feature of judge, member of parliament

parts.note: a group of owls is called a parliament, so one owl is a member of it

explanation.surface: A feature of a judge or a politician's well-fed face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of parliament' suggests an MP; here it is one bird of a parliament of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose flesh under the jaw is a fleshy part of the face.
